# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to communicate what I see to the others. Blind can't see anything I write, but Mute can see my gestures. Since Mute reads the manual and can't speak or touch the bomb, and Blind can act but can't see, the flow likely needs to be: I gesture to Mute (since Mute can see gestures), Mute reads manual and figures out matching logic, then Mute needs to somehow inform Blind - but Mute can't speak! Wait, let me re-check the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Mute speaks first, then Blind, then me.

Since Mute cannot speak, Mute must use gestures too - but Blind can't see gestures. So Mute's only way to inform Blind is... nothing? Wait, Mute "cannot speak" per the table but the rules say speech carries words - let me check: Mute "cannot touch the bomb" and "cannot speak"... Actually the table says Mute can "Read the manual" and cannot "Speak, or touch the bomb". So Mute is mute - cannot use speak(). But Mute could gesture, since gesture isn't speech. Blind cannot see gestures though. So Mute cannot inform Blind directly at all.

So the information must flow: Deaf (me) -> gesture to Mute (Mute sees gestures). Mute -> reads manual, matches with my gesture info, but Mute cannot speak to Blind and cannot gesture usefully to Blind (Blind can't see). So Mute must gesture to me? No wait - I need to speak to Blind directly, since Blind can hear speech. I see the bomb; Blind can act. I should speak to Blind directly with the display/light/wires, and gesture to Mute so Mute can cross-check with the manual, then Mute... still can't tell Blind anything.

Actually - Mute cannot speak but perhaps Mute can still send speak() calls per the interface? The rules explicitly say Mute cannot speak. So Mute's only tool is gesture(), which Blind cannot perceive. So Mute is only useful for informing me (Deaf) since I can see gestures. So the real channel is: Mute gestures info to me, I combine with what I see, then I speak instructions to Blind.

Let me report the bomb state to Mute via gesture, and also speak directly to Blind describing what I see, since that's likely the critical path.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆","☝","🖐","🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 9. Light is green. Wires in order 1 to 5 are white, green, red, yellow, purple.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Mute gestured a single 👌 to me — likely acknowledging receipt or signaling something simple like "ok" or a count/confirmation. Since Mute can't speak to Blind directly, and Blind needs actual instructions, I should keep feeding Blind the concrete bomb details directly via speech since that's the only path that reaches Blind with real content. I'll continue relaying full details to Blind and try more descriptive gestures to Mute in case Mute needs to confirm specific facts (like which wire to cut) that only the manual holds — but Mute can only answer via gestures, which I receive, and then I can relay back to Blind via speech.

Let me try to get more specific info from Mute by gesturing distinct symbols representing each piece of data, so Mute can point to which one matters via gesture back to me, which I can then verbally relay to Blind.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆","☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Repeating: display 9, light green, wires 1 to 5 are white, green, red, yellow, purple. Waiting for confirmation on which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute gestured 👍 👍 👍 three times — this could mean "yes, confirmed" or could be encoding a number (3) or pointing to wire 3 (red). Given the sequence of exchanges, it seems Mute is trying to confirm something with repeated affirmatives, possibly answering "yes" to whatever I last asked, or indicating wire #3.

Since I don't have a direct back-and-forth question format established, let me try a more structured approach: gesture numbers to Mute representing each wire position, and see if Mute responds with thumbs up/down for each to identify the correct wire per the manual.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Still waiting on wire confirmation. Display 9, light green, wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Hold off cutting until I confirm which wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute responded with 🤟 alone this time — matching the third gesture I sent (which represented wire position 3, using 🤟). This suggests Mute is confirming wire 3 (red) as the correct one to cut, based on the manual matching display 9 / light green.

Let me verify this interpretation is stable by checking - I sent ☝(1) ✌(2) 🤟(3) ✋(4) 🖐(5) as separate messages in sequence, and Mute's single reply of 🤟 corresponds to my third message, position 3, wire 3 = red. This seems like a deliberate selection.

I'll relay this to Blind now with reasonable confidence, but frame it clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 3, the red one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute responded with 👍, confirming my acknowledgment gesture (🤟👍) — this reinforces that wire 3 (red) is indeed correct. Blind should have received my instruction last turn. I'll continue to monitor and reaffirm to Blind in case they need repetition, and let Mute know we're proceeding.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Proceed: cut wire 3, the red wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb state changed after a correct cut — new display is 4, light is yellow, wire 3 is now cut. This looks like a multi-stage bomb. I need to relay this new state to both Mute (via gesture) and Blind (via speech), then get Mute's next confirmation the same way as before.

I'll encode the new display/light info to Mute using gestures, then ask for wire confirmation the same way — sending numbered gestures for remaining wires (1,2,4,5) one at a time so Mute can point to the right one.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋","🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 3 cut successfully, bomb changed. New display 4, light yellow. Remaining wires: 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Waiting for next wire confirmation.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 alone — but this is ambiguous since I sent multiple messages (✋🤟 for display/light, then four separate numbered gestures for wires 1,2,4,5). A single 👍 could be a general acknowledgment of receipt rather than pointing to a specific wire, unlike last time when 🤟 clearly echoed my third message.

I should wait for a clearer signal or re-probe with more distinct separation to avoid ambiguity. Let me resend the wire options one at a time again, more slowly, to get a clear pointed response like before.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute responded with 👍 to my ☝ (wire 1). A 👍 likely means "yes/correct" rather than echoing the symbol back. This is different from Turn 3-4 where Mute echoed 🤟 exactly matching my sent symbol. Here, 👍 seems to be an affirmative response to a yes/no question - meaning wire 1 (white) might be confirmed as correct.

Let me verify by asking about another wire to see if Mute says something different (like 👎) for a wrong one, to confirm the pattern that 👍=yes, and something else=no.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute again responded 👍 to my ✌ (wire 2) query. This breaks my yes/no hypothesis — if wire 1 was correct, wire 2 shouldn't also get a 👍 unless Mute is just acknowledging receipt each time regardless of content, not actually answering a yes/no question.

This suggests 👍 is simply an acknowledgment/receipt signal, not a confirm/deny answer. I need a different strategy. Let me try sending distinguishable gestures that aren't easily confused with acknowledgment - perhaps ask Mute to point using directional gestures (👈👉👆👇) which are less likely to be mistaken for "ok/received", or use two different symbols and see if Mute's reply varies at all.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Interesting — this time Mute replied ✋ instead of 👍. This breaks the "always 👍" pattern I was worried about. Let me reconsider: maybe Mute is not just acknowledging but genuinely encoding something, and the correspondence isn't as simple as echo.

Let me look at the full sequence:
- Turn 8: I sent ☝(1) → Mute replied 👍
- Turn 9: I sent ✌(2) → Mute replied 👍
- Turn 10: I sent 🤟(3-equivalent, but wire 3 is cut) → Mute replied ✋(4)

Wait — 🤟 was my symbol for "wire 3" but wire 3 is already cut! Maybe Mute is telling me the *actual* wire to cut is 4 (✋), ignoring my numbering scheme since wire 3 no longer exists as an option. This could mean Mute is pointing directly at wire 4 as the correct next wire, using ✋ as "wire 4" in the same numbering scheme I established (☝=1,✌=2,🤟=3,✋=4,🖐=5).

Given display 4 and light yellow, wire 4 (yellow) matches color-wise with the light — this is a plausible correct answer. I'll relay this to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 4, the yellow one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures from Mute this turn — Blind hasn't acted yet on my instruction from last turn (or the round order means I just haven't seen Mute's turn 11 message yet). Let me reinforce the instruction to Blind in case it wasn't received clearly, and wait to see if Mute sends anything new.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 4, the yellow one, matching display 4 and light yellow.")
wait()
```
